chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no inheritance for the killer'.
ai.seo_question: Does a killer inherit from their victim in Islam?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ghulul' (exclusion) in inheritance, where a killer is barred from inheriting from their victim to prevent unjust enrichment. Shia jurists, including Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi, have extensively debated whether this disqualification is absolute or subject to specific conditions, such as the type of homicide (murder vs. manslaughter). It serves as a critical link between Prophetic tradition and the detailed application of inheritance law in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is no inheritance for the killer’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad and ‘Abd Allah sons of Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
has said that a murderer cannot receive inheritance.’”
